items.prompt: A matrix has rows (3, 1) and (2, 4). What is its determinant?
items.hint: Multiply the pair on the main diagonal, then subtract the product of the other pair: ad − bc.
items.explain: ad − bc with a = 3, b = 1, c = 2 and d = 4 gives {answer}. The unit square’s area is multiplied by that.

items.prompt: A matrix has rows (2, 4) and (1, 2). What is its determinant?
items.hint: Compare the two columns, (2, 1) and (4, 2). Do they point the same way?
items.explain: ad − bc gives {answer}. The second column is twice the first, so the square is squashed flat and the matrix has no inverse.

items.prompt: A copier prints a page at the same size, but with left and right swapped, as if read through the back of the sheet. What does its matrix’s determinant look like?

choices.text: Negative, with an absolute value of 1
choices.why: The size is kept, so the absolute value is 1, and the flip makes it negative.

choices.text: Zero, because left and right swap
choices.why: Zero would mean the page is flattened to a line. Swapping left and right keeps every part of the page; it only reverses the orientation.

choices.text: Positive, because no area is lost
choices.why: No area is lost, but a positive determinant also means the orientation is kept. A mirror image reverses it.

items.prompt: Before you continue, predict: if the two columns point along the same line, what is the area of the parallelogram?
items.reasoning: Zero. Both sides of the parallelogram lie along one line, so it is flat, and ad − bc is 0 for any such pair of columns. A matrix like that squashes the whole square onto a line, so it has no inverse.
